subject: business-studies
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 have two parts of 1 mark each.
Section C: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) A profession requires specialised knowledge and training. (b) Regularity of dealings is not necessary for an activity to be called business.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — business requires regular dealings.

questions.q: Identify the type of industry: (a) It is concerned with the production of goods with the help of nature. (b) It is engaged in reproducing and multiplying certain species of plants and animals for sale.
questions.answer:
(a) Primary industry
(b) Genetic industry

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) An LLP has a ________ legal identity from its partners. (b) A partnership requires a minimum of ________ persons.
questions.answer:
(a) separate
(b) two

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Death, bankruptcy or insanity of members does not affect the continuity of a cooperative society. (b) A cooperative society can be started with a minimum of 2 members.
questions.answer:
(a) True — it has a separate legal entity and stable life.
(b) False — it needs at least 10 members.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Domestic producers improve the quality of their products because of multinational companies. (b) It is necessary to get every company incorporated, whether private or public.
questions.answer:
(a) True — competition from MNCs pushes them to improve.
(b) True — registration under the Companies Act is compulsory.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Walking with a straight body posture shows ________. (b) ________ communication flows through officially prescribed channels.
questions.answer:
(a) confidence
(b) Formal

questions.q: Give one-word answers: (a) Who receives the message? (b) What is exchanged in communication?
questions.answer:
(a) The receiver.
(b) Information (the message — facts, ideas, opinions).

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Deposits in a savings bank account serve present as well as future needs. (b) A fixed amount must be deposited every month in a Fixed Deposit Account.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — that is a recurring deposit; an FD is a single lump sum for a fixed period.

questions.q: A company took a fire policy of ₹7 lakh. Three months later a fire caused a loss of ₹3 lakh. (a) How much will it get? (b) Which principle applies?
questions.answer:
(a) ₹3 lakh — the actual loss.
(b) Principle of indemnity.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Wholesalers require a small amount of capital. (b) A channel of distribution is the route taken by goods from producers to consumers.
questions.answer:
(a) False — they need a large amount of capital.
(b) True

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Television advertising is more effective because it has ________ impact. (b) Periodicals have a longer ________ than newspapers.
questions.answer:
(a) audio-visual
(b) life

questions.q: Mr. Rajeev was crippled for life because of a doctor's negligence during treatment. (a) Which consumer right was violated? (b) What can he do?
questions.answer:
(a) Right to safety.
(b) Exercise his right to seek redressal — file a complaint for compensation in the consumer commission.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) The National Commission consists of a President and six other members. (b) Consumer awareness means making consumers aware of their rights and liabilities.
questions.answer:
(a) False — under the 1986 Act it had a President and at least four members.
(b) True

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) ________ employment means serving another person for wages or salary. (b) When a person engages in an economic activity and manages it on his own, it is known as ________.
questions.answer:
(a) Wage
(b) self-employment

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Only rich persons can start a business. (b) An entrepreneur should start a retail business far away from customers' residences.
questions.answer:
(a) False — anyone can start a small business.
(b) False — a retail shop should be near residential areas or a market.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are aids to trade? Name any four.
questions.answer: Activities that remove the hindrances in the flow of goods from producers to consumers. Transport, warehousing, insurance, advertising (and banking).

questions.q: Explain teleconferencing and audio-conferencing.
questions.answer:
Teleconferencing is a system through which people interact without physically sitting together, using telephone, computers or television.
Audio-conferencing is two-way voice communication — participants at different places hear each other and respond immediately.

questions.q: Mahesh's father wants to save ₹2,00,000 to gift Mahesh on his graduation day. Which deposit should he open?
questions.answer: A fixed deposit account — a lump sum is deposited for a fixed period and earns a higher rate of interest.

questions.q: State any two functions of a retailer.
questions.answer:
(1) Buying and assembling a variety of goods from many suppliers.
(2) Personal service — advice and home delivery; also credit to regular customers, display and storage of goods.

or.q: What is a direct channel? Give two examples.
or.answer: A channel in which the producer sells directly to the consumer without any middleman. Examples: Bata selling through its own shops; banking, insurance and telephone services; door-to-door selling.

questions.q: What is meant by advertising? State two of its features.
questions.answer:
Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods and services by an identified sponsor.
Features: (1) it is paid; (2) the sponsor is identified (also non-personal, carried through media).

questions.q: Explain any two possible areas of self-employment with two examples each.
questions.answer:
(1) Small-scale retail business — grocery store, stationery shop.
(2) Services based on skill — tailoring, cycle and scooter repair.
(Also professions, small farming, cottage industries, arts and crafts.)

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: 'A sole proprietorship is the best form of organisation if the owner can handle everything.' Explain any five advantages of sole proprietorship.
questions.answer:
(1) Easy to form and close — few legal formalities.
(2) Quick decisions — the owner need not consult anyone.
(3) Direct motivation — all the profit goes to the owner, so he works hard.
(4) Secrecy — business information stays with the owner.
(5) Personal contact with customers and employees, and flexibility to change with the market.

questions.q: Explain two types of cooperative banks. OR Explain the different modes of payment.
questions.answer:
Cooperative banks: (1) Primary credit societies — village-level societies giving small loans to members; (2) Central cooperative banks — district-level, finance the primary societies; (3) State cooperative banks — apex bank of the state.
Modes of payment: cash, cheque, demand draft, debit and credit cards, net banking and UPI transfers.

questions.q: What is television advertising? Explain any two advantages.
questions.answer:
Television advertising means showing advertisements on TV channels during breaks or in sponsored programmes.
(1) Audio-visual impact — products can be seen, heard and demonstrated, so it is the most effective medium.
(2) Lasting impact and wide reach — catchy slogans, music and celebrities are remembered; it reaches even illiterate viewers through regional channels.

questions.q: What is meant by consumerism? Explain any one responsibility of consumers.
questions.answer:
Consumerism is a movement by consumers to ensure fair and honest practices by sellers and to protect themselves from exploitation.
Responsibility — proof of transaction: the consumer must always obtain and preserve the cash memo and warranty card, without which a claim for repair or replacement cannot be established.

questions.q: How does self-employment help reduce unemployment?
questions.answer:
(1) The person employs himself instead of looking for a job.
(2) A growing self-employed business hires assistants and workers, creating more jobs.
(3) It promotes small and cottage industries in villages, giving local employment and reducing migration.

or.q: State three examples of self-employment based on professional qualifications.
or.answer: A doctor running a private clinic; a lawyer practising in courts; a chartered accountant (or architect) with his own office.

questions.q: What are the sources of finance for setting up a small business?
questions.answer:
(1) Own savings (self-contribution).
(2) Loans from friends and relatives.
(3) Loans from banks and financial institutions, and government schemes such as MUDRA and SIDBI.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What are national objectives of business? Explain four of them.
questions.answer:
National objectives are goals business pursues for the progress of the country.
(1) Generating employment for the people.
(2) Promoting social justice — equal opportunity to all, help to weaker sections.
(3) Producing according to national priorities — goods needed by the nation, as in the plans.
(4) Contributing to government revenue by paying taxes honestly; also self-sufficiency and export promotion.

questions.q: Explain any three advantages and two limitations of joint stock companies.
questions.answer:
Advantages: (1) Large capital from many shareholders. (2) Limited liability encourages investment. (3) Perpetual succession and transferability of shares; professional management.
Limitations: (1) Difficult, costly formation and excessive legal control. (2) Delay in decisions and lack of secrecy.

questions.q: What is marine insurance? Explain cargo, hull and freight insurance.
questions.answer:
Marine insurance is a contract by which the insurer (underwriter) indemnifies the owner of a ship or cargo against perils of the sea.
Cargo insurance — covers the goods carried against loss by storm, sinking, etc.
Hull insurance — covers the ship itself.
Freight insurance — covers loss of the freight the shipping company would earn if the cargo is lost or damaged.

questions.q: Who is a consumer? Explain the various responsibilities of a consumer.
questions.answer:
A consumer is a person who buys goods or services for his own use or for others on his behalf, not for resale.
(1) Self-help — be well informed and alert.
(2) Proof of transaction — obtain and keep cash memos and warranty cards.
(3) Proper claim — make only reasonable claims.
(4) Proper use of products — do not misuse goods under guarantee.
(5) Awareness of rights, checking quality marks and MRP, honouring agreements and timely payment, avoiding pirated goods.
